items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I was very disappointed with they replaced him with Sonny Payne, although I could see why they did it. Sonny was a showman.

ctx.x: What was it about that rhythm section that made it so identifiable?

Well by that time of course I had memorized the Basie records. That was one of the things Buzzy did for me when I first met him in Seattle, was he said, “You don’t know about the Count Basie band?” He got out all the, especially the old Deccas with Lester on them, and played me all of those things. And he listened to me play drums a couple of times when I was at jam sessions and things, and he liked the way I played well enough to send me in to sub for him, because he knew I didn’t play as well as he did and I…

in rhythmic terms, and I just, it was like the scales fell from my eyes, I saw immediately what he was talking about. And from then on I had some kind of an ideal, rhythmically, to shoot for. So that was when I got to hear this version of the Basie band, I thought Gus Johnson was ideal, because he was doing the same kind of thing in the rhythm section. Gus had an interesting style of playing his cymbal beat was kind of up on the top of the beat. And it wasn’t a loose, you know, the way the time is divided in…
